subject: SS
title: Egypt map studio: locate all 14 places and explain the relationships
teach: This original training schematic is north-up and not to scale. It teaches relative locations; never use its spacing to calculate distance. Nearby Memphis and Giza, and Thebes and the Valley of the Kings, are deliberately separated for readable labels.

Upper Egypt is upstream in the south; Lower Egypt is downstream in the north. Follow the Nile north to the branching Delta and Mediterranean. Upstream is a river relationship, not the top of the page.

Use the seas and river as anchors: Mediterranean north, Red Sea east, Nile through the land. Sinai is northeast between the branches near the head of the Red Sea; Nubia lies south along the river. The Western Desert lies west of the Nile. The worksheet label Western Sahara Desert at that location must not be confused with the modern Western Sahara territory far to the west.

Memphis lies near the Delta head. Giza is nearby and west of the Nile. Thebes lies farther south, with the Valley of the Kings nearby to the west. Alexandria lies on the Mediterranean coast and was founded much later than the Old Kingdom. Place and historical period belong together.
Cover the model, then rebuild the anchors and add the other labels from memory. Explain how you know each location. Fresh check maps change the letters so memorizing a letter will not work.

model.prompt: Trace a route from Nubia to Thebes, Memphis, the Delta and the Mediterranean. What stays the same as the place names change?
model.reasoning: Start in the south at Nubia. Follow the river generally north past the Thebes area, then toward Memphis near the Delta head. Continue through the Delta toward the Mediterranean. You keep moving downstream while moving up a north-up page.
model.answer: The route moves generally north and downstream. Upper/Lower describe river position, not the top and bottom of the page.

guided.prompt: Why can this map teach location relationships but not an exact Memphis-to-Thebes distance?
options: The schematic is not to scale.
The places are all at the same location.
Historical places have no spatial relationships.
guided.rationale: Schematic spacing is deliberately simplified. Use a scaled map for distance.

teachingSections.title: Explain each location
teach: This original training schematic is north-up and not to scale. It teaches relative locations; never use its spacing to calculate distance. Nearby Memphis and Giza, and Thebes and the Valley of the Kings, are deliberately separated for readable labels.

Upper Egypt is upstream in the south; Lower Egypt is downstream in the north. Follow the Nile north to the branching Delta and Mediterranean. Upstream is a river relationship, not the top of the page.

Use the seas and river as anchors: Mediterranean north, Red Sea east, Nile through the land. Sinai is northeast between the branches near the head of the Red Sea; Nubia lies south along the river. The Western Desert lies west of the Nile. The worksheet label Western Sahara Desert at that location must not be confused with the modern Western Sahara territory far to the west.

Memphis lies near the Delta head. Giza is nearby and west of the Nile. Thebes lies farther south, with the Valley of the Kings nearby to the west. Alexandria lies on the Mediterranean coast and was founded much later than the Old Kingdom. Place and historical period belong together.

example.prompt: How can you locate the Valley of the Kings without remembering a letter?

example.why: It uses the place relationship rather than a memorized letter.
